disclaimer: Drafted from real web search results against named official/authoritative sources for Singapore (2026), as an engineering starting point. This is NOT verified legal compliance and NOT a substitute for review by qualified legal counsel before relying on it for any real compliance purpose. Every rule's action is deliberately set to Log only (never Block/Warn/RequireConfirmation) since this content has not been reviewed by counsel. Fast-moving amendments are not tracked automatically here — verify currency against the cited source before relying on this. Expanded 2026-10-27 via live web search (domains: sso.agc.gov.sg, pdpc.gov.sg, csa.gov.sg, mddi.gov.sg, ipos.gov.sg, mha.gov.sg, police.gov.sg); statute pages on sso.agc.gov.sg returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch, so snippets for those rules come from the search results' retrieved excerpts, not full statute text. All added rules are Log only.

rules.source: Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (PDPA), administered by the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC). Official: https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/organisations/regulations-decisions/personal-data-protection-act-pdpa
rules.retrieved_snippet: The Singapore Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (PDPA) is the data privacy law in Singapore that regulates the collection, management, and disclosure to third parties of personal data by businesses and individuals... maximum financial penalty for non-compliance could reach one million SGD, or 10% of the organization's turnover.

rules.source: Code of Practice for Online Safety, issued by the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), effective July 18 2023 — requires designated Social Media Services to protect users including children from harmful content. Official: https://www.imda.gov.sg/resources/press-releases-factsheets-and-speeches/press-releases/2023/imdas-online-safety-code-comes-into-effect
rules.retrieved_snippet: IMDA has issued a Code of Practice for Online Safety which takes effect from 18 July 2023, requiring designated Social Media Services to enhance online safety in Singapore and curb the spread of harmful content, especially protecting children... Failure to comply with the Code may result in fines of up to SGD 1 million.

rules.source: Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act (CPFTA), including Lemon Law provisions (Part III). Official ministry reference: https://www.mti.gov.sg/newsroom/public-consultation-lemon-law
rules.retrieved_snippet: "Lemon laws" refer to consumer protection laws that provide remedies for consumers against latent defects in goods... The Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act (CPFTA) and the Lemon Law (Part III) provide repair, replacement, price reduction, or refund — with a defect that shows up within 6 months presumed to have existed at delivery.

rules.source: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI, released by the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), first issued 22 Jan 2026 (World Economic Forum), updated 20 May 2026 — voluntary/soft-law, risk-based, requiring meaningful human accountability and oversight (human-approval checkpoints for actions with material real-world impact). Third edition after Traditional AI (2020) and Generative AI (2024) frameworks. Official: https://www.imda.gov.sg/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Singapore unveiled its Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI on January 22, 2026 — the world's first comprehensive governance framework for agentic AI systems... predominantly soft-law, risk-based, and sector-specific... requiring humans to remain ultimately accountable for agents' actions, necessitating effective human oversight mechanisms including significant checkpoints where human approval is required for actions with material real-world impacts.

rules.source: No mandatory private-sector digital accessibility law — IMDA's Accessibility Guidelines strongly recommend (not enforce) WCAG 2.1 Level AA. Government sector is mandatory: Singapore's Digital Service Standards require WCAG 2.1 AA for public agencies; the Enabling Masterplan 2030 targets all high-traffic government websites accessible by 2030 (61% as of search). Honest gap: no enforceable private-sector standard exists yet. Secondary summary: https://peopleofinternet.com/articles/singapore-mandates-digital-accessibility-for-government-serv.html ; official: https://www.imda.gov.sg/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Singapore's Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) provides Accessibility Guidelines that recommend WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance for digital services. However, Singapore currently has no mandatory private sector digital accessibility law... government agencies face mandatory compliance requirements for WCAG 2.1 AA standards. The Enabling Masterplan 2030 sets the goal of ensuring that all high-traffic government websites are fully accessible by 2030, up from the current 61%.

rules.source: Personal Data Protection Act 2012, section 26D (notification of notifiable data breaches) — https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/PDPA2012?ProvIds=P16A- ; PDPC guidance https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/organisations/e-services/report-your-organisations-data-breach
rules.retrieved_snippet: Section 26D(1) requires an organisation to notify the Commission as soon as practicable, and no later than 3 calendar days after the day it assesses the breach as notifiable; a breach is notifiable if likely to cause significant harm or if it affects 500 or more individuals. (An older PDPC document giving a 72-hour window is superseded.)

Part 2 covers offences, starting with unauthorised access to computer material (section 3); section 4 covers access with intent to commit a further offence; the Act also covers modification, interception, obstruction and disclosure of access codes. Current consolidation amended by Act 16 of 2023, effective 8 February 2024.

rules.source: Cybersecurity Act 2018 (as amended by the Cybersecurity (Amendment) Act 2024) — https://www.csa.gov.sg/legislation/cybersecurity-act/
rules.retrieved_snippet: "CII are computer systems directly involved in the provision of essential services"; the Act provides a framework for the designation of CII. Per CSA, the Cybersecurity (Amendment) Act's key provisions took effect 31 October 2025, adding Systems of Temporary Cybersecurity Concern, Entities of Special Cybersecurity Interest and Foundational Digital Infrastructure; CSA states owners of provider-owned CII must notify CSA within 2 hours of an incident.

rules.source: Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act 2019 (POFMA) — https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/POFMA2019 ; POFMA Office https://www.pofmaoffice.gov.sg/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Took effect 2 October 2019; administered by the POFMA Office within IMDA. Main tools are Correction Directions (no removal required) and, in more serious cases, stop-communication or disabling directions; persistent disseminators may be designated Declared Online Locations. MDDI states a Correction Direction can also apply to online falsehoods communicated via deepfake videos.

rules.source: Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act 2025 (Act 23 of 2025) — https://www.mddi.gov.sg/newsroom/online-safety-commission-and-online-safety--relief-and-accountability--act-2025-to-start-on-29-june-2026/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Passed 5 November 2025; MDDI announced the Online Safety Commission would begin operations 29 June 2026. First phase covers online harassment (including online sexual harassment), doxxing, online stalking, intimate image abuse and image-based child abuse; the Commissioner can direct takedown or account restriction, and non-compliance with directions is a criminal offence.

rules.source: Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising) (Amendment) Act 2024 (No. 34 of 2024) — https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Acts-Supp/34-2024/Published/20241121?DocDate=20241121 ; MDDI https://www.mddi.gov.sg/newsroom/new-legal-measures-uphold-integrity-online-advertising-elections/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Prohibits publishing digitally generated or manipulated online election advertising that realistically depicts a candidate saying or doing something they did not, from issuance of the Writ to close of polling; limited to candidates; commenced 22 January 2025 per the search results. Penalty amounts were not retrieved.

rules.source: Corruption, Drug Trafficking and Other Serious Crimes (Confiscation of Benefits) Act 1992 (CDSA), as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Other Matters Act 2024 — https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/CDTOSCCBA1992 ; Singapore Police Force release https://www.police.gov.sg/media-hub/news/2026/02/20260206_woman_sentenced_to_21_months_imprisonment_for_money_laundering_offences
rules.retrieved_snippet: SSO lists the CDSA as current as at 26 October 2026; contents cover confiscation orders, production orders and offences. Police releases describe money laundering charges under section 54 (possession/concealment of criminal benefits) and section 55 (reasonable-suspicion possession); a section 54(3A) transfer offence took effect 8 February 2024.

rules.source: Terrorism (Suppression of Financing) Act 2002 (Act 16 of 2002) — https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/TSFA2002 ; MHA https://www.mha.gov.sg/what-we-do/managing-security-threats/countering-the-financing-of-terrorism/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Act 16 of 2002 (2020 Revised Edition in force 31 December 2021; long title refers to the International Convention for the Suppression of the Financing of Terrorism). The First Schedule (No. 3) Order 2025 added a listed person, operative 18 July 2025.

rules.source: Copyright Act 2021 (ss 243-244 computational data analysis; s 187) — https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Acts-Supp/22-2021/Published/20211231?DocDate=20211007 ; IPOS https://www.ipos.gov.sg/news/news-collection/commencement-of-the-copyright-act/
rules.retrieved_snippet: In force 21 November 2021. Section 243 defines computational data analysis (including using works as training examples for software); section 244 permits copying for it subject to lawful access and no other purpose; contract terms excluding the permitted use are void under section 187. A 2026 MinLaw/IPOS consultation asks whether the exception's scope for AI training is clear (reform status unconfirmed).

rules.source: Gambling Control Act 2022 (No. 15 of 2022) — https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/GCA2022 ; MHA https://www.mha.gov.sg/what-we-do/maintaining-law-and-order/regulating-casino-and-gambling-industry/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Passed 11 March 2022, effective 1 August 2022; consolidated the Betting Act, Common Gaming Houses Act, Private Lotteries Act and Remote Gambling Act. Has a dedicated division on remote gambling and a power to block access to online locations; offences apply even if offenders reside overseas, as long as customers are in Singapore.
